name: phrase-matching
title: phrase-matching: which documents contain a quoted phrase, adjacent and in order
interface:
Module `lib/phrase.mjs`.

```stub
export function quotedPhrases(raw: string): string[][];
export function phraseDocs(reader: object, terms: string[]): number[];
export function phraseDocIds(reader: object, phrases: string[][]): Set<string> | null;
```

- `quotedPhrases(raw)` returns the CLOSED double-quoted segments of a raw query string, each
  tokenized with text-analyzer's `tokenize`, in order. Text outside quotes yields nothing; a
  quote that is never closed is not a phrase (the query degrades to ordinary term search); a
  segment with no tokens ("", " - ") is dropped rather than made unsatisfiable. A string with
  no quotes, or a non-string, yields [].
- `phraseDocs(reader, terms)` returns the indices, ascending, of the documents where `terms`
  occur ADJACENT and IN ORDER — consecutive positions, per the reader's position space, which
  forbids a match straddling title and body. A one-term phrase is that term's documents. An
  empty phrase, a phrase naming a term the index does not hold, and an empty index all yield [].
  It must not touch the filesystem: any object with docCount/docId/postings-with-positions works.
- `phraseDocIds(reader, phrases)` returns the ids of the documents satisfying EVERY phrase, or
  null when there is no phrase at all. null ("do not restrict") and the empty Set ("nothing can
  match") are different answers and must not be conflated.
nl_description: Exact-phrase search as a filter rather than a second scorer: a query wrapped in double quotes narrows the candidate documents to those containing the phrase, and bm25-ranking then orders that restricted set exactly as it orders everything else. Keeping matching and scoring apart is what keeps relevance tuning in one place. Reusable by anything that needs adjacency over the positional index reader.
